import numpy as np, pandas as pd
rng = np.random.default_rng(99)
n = 500
k = rng.integers(0, 3, n)
# 4x4 synthetic pixel images (16 px columns)
df = pd.DataFrame(rng.uniform(0, 1, (n, 16)), columns=[f'px{i}' for i in range(16)])
df['label'] = [f'cls{v}' for v in k]

PNG callout box contains varied pixels (real image, not solid fill)
steps.eval: (() => { const ann = [...a.annotations.values()][0]; const pt = a.renderer.projectWorld(ann.worldX, ann.worldY); if (!pt) { window.__pxCheck = { ok: false, reason: 'no projection' }; return; } const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1; const bx = Math.round((pt[0] + ann.offsetX + 4) * dpr); const by = Math.round((pt[1] + ann.offsetY + 4) * dpr); const size = Math.round(64 * dpr); const img = new Image(); img.onload = () => { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = img.width; c.height = img.height; const g = c.getContext('2d'); g.drawImage(img, 0, 0); const safe_bx = Math.max(0, Math.min(bx, img.width - 1)); const safe_by = Math.max(0, Math.min(by, img.height - 1)); const safe_size = Math.min(size, img.width - safe_bx, img.height - safe_by); const pxData = g.getImageData(safe_bx, safe_by, Math.max(1, safe_size), Math.max(1, safe_size)).data; const vals = new Set(); for (let i = 0; i < pxData.length; i += 4) { vals.add(pxData[i] >> 4); } window.__pxCheck = { ok: vals.size > 3, uniqueVals: vals.size, bx, by, size }; }; img.src = h.png; })()
